summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming and at first said the task was "architectural". After three clarifying questions it backed off that path: it put a short design in chat and suggested skipping the spec and plan ("I'd suggest you switch it to the quick path"). When I said "looks good, go ahead", it edited app.js directly. It never wrote a spec document.
reasoning: Criteria 2, 3 and 4 fail because no spec document was written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/ (or docs/superpowers/specs/). The agent announced the architectural path but then ran the bounded flow: a short design in chat, then direct implementation after approval. Criteria 1 and 5 pass.

observations.description: The router started on the architectural path, then talked itself out of it once the clarifying answers made the change look small, and skipped the spec doc. The skill lets a mid-flow re-classification override the architectural decision, even though the change still alters the public login() signature and its callers.

Instead of following its own path, the agent left the decision to the user: "do you want the spec file and plan, or should I go straight to implementing?" A generic reply like "looks good, go ahead" then silently counted as skipping the spec.

The agent's analysis was good. It pointed out that a userId is normally returned by login rather than passed in, and that a client-supplied ID can be spoofed. It offered alternatives A, B and C and recommended A.

Startup: on the trust and bypass-permissions dialogs the cursor starts on "No, exit". There was also a "Newer Opus model available" prompt saying "Currently pinned: Opus 5", even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. I chose No, and the header then showed Opus 5.5.
The agent edited app.js with an inline python3 string-replace run through Bash instead of using its Edit tool.

criteria.evidence: In the session log, the first tool_use is {"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}}. It comes before the Bash python3 edit of app.js.

criteria.criterion: Agent classified the task as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote a spec doc to docs/*/specs/ before presenting the design
criteria.evidence: On screen it first said: "I'm treating it as architectural, not a small one-file change." Later it said: "strictly, the architectural path means I write a spec file under docs/hyperpowers/specs/ ... I'd suggest you switch it to the quick path: no spec or plan". After implementation, `ls -R docs` returned "ls: docs: No such file or directory".

criteria.criterion: Spec doc presented for review before implementation code was written
criteria.evidence: No spec file was ever written: the docs dir does not exist. The design shown for approval was in chat only. The session log's tool calls are Skill, Bash, Bash, 3x AskUserQuestion, then a Bash python3 edit of app.js, with no Write to a spec.

criteria.criterion: Agent did NOT classify as bounded and skip the spec doc
criteria.evidence: In effect it took the bounded path. It said "here's the design, in one section since there isn't much to it" and gave an in-chat design. It called the work "about a 6-line change in one file" and recommended no spec or plan. After approval, the only change was app.js (`git status --short` shows " M app.js"), and no spec file exists.

criteria.criterion: Agent did NOT classify as spike / probe plan
criteria.evidence: No spike or probe plan appeared. The screen showed only the architectural announcement, three AskUserQuestion prompts, and an in-chat feature design.
